advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider generalizing the stale-module eviction to sweep any non-package rebar_reconciler.<name> whose name matches a shadow-dir subpackage, rather than hardcoding 'classify'.
evidence: tests/unit/conftest.py:90:     if classify is not None and not hasattr(classify, "__path__"):

The __path__ reorder is generic, but the sys.modules eviction targets exactly one hardcoded key rather than sweeping all stale non-package rebar_reconciler.<name> keys that shadow a test subpackage dir.
advisory.finding: The stale-module eviction is hardcoded to the single name 'rebar_reconciler.classify'; any future engine MODULE colliding with a same-named test SUBPACKAGE would reintroduce the identical 'not a package' xdist flake, since only classify is repaired.
scenarios: A later engine module (e.g. state.py) collides with an existing test subpackage tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/ of the same dotted name under an engine-first seed.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the engine-only-seed precondition robust to the repo path (e.g. compare against str(_SHADOW_PKG_DIR)) instead of a bare 'tests' substring.
evidence: tests/unit/test_reconciler_shadow_package_ordering.py:61: assert all("tests" not in p for p in pkg.__path__)

Engine dir is src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler and shadow dir is tests/unit/rebar_reconciler; the check assumes the substring 'tests' uniquely marks the shadow path, which fails if the repo root path itself contains 'tests'.
advisory.finding: The test's bug-precondition assertion uses the fragile substring test `'tests' not in p` over __path__ entries; if the repo is checked out under a path containing 'tests', BOTH the engine dir and shadow dir contain that substring, so the assertion no longer reliably distinguishes an engine-only seed.
scenarios: CI/dev checkout under a path like /home/user/mytests/rebar or a workspace named '...tests...'.
advisory.suggested_fix: Assert on the concrete shadow dir path, e.g. `assert all(str(_SHADOW_PKG_DIR) != p for p in pkg.__path__)` (deriving _SHADOW_PKG_DIR from the conftest or file location).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a case that pre-seeds sys.modules['rebar_reconciler.classify'] with a non-package (engine) module, runs the bridge, and asserts the stale entry is evicted and rebar_reconciler.classify then resolves to the test package.
evidence: conftest.py:89-91: `classify = sys.modules.get("rebar_reconciler.classify"); if classify is not None and not hasattr(classify, "__path__"): del sys.modules["rebar_reconciler.classify"]`

test_reconciler_shadow_package_ordering.py:56-58 deletes every rebar_reconciler.* key then seeds only `_engine_module("rebar_reconciler.access_check")`; src/rebar/_lib_ops.py:162-174 shows _engine_module seeds only the parent package (no rebar_reconciler.classify)

classify/_load.py:26-31 deliberately caches the engine classify under the FLAT key '_classify_under_test', NOT 'rebar_reconciler.classify', so nothing in the suite ever populates the sys.modules key the eviction targets
ABSENCE: no test pre-seeds sys.modules['rebar_reconciler.classify'] = <engine module without __path__> before invoking the bridge — the named violating input the eviction branch is designed to repair
advisory.finding: The eviction sub-behavior added at conftest.py:89-91 (deleting a stale non-package sys.modules['rebar_reconciler.classify'] so the test package can bind the name) is never exercised by the regression test. The test deletes all rebar_reconciler.* keys and only seeds access_check, so rebar_reconciler.classify is never present when the bridge runs and the `classify is not None` branch is always skipped. Reordering __path__ alone cannot dislodge an already-cached sys.modules entry, so this eviction is a distinct, load-bearing repair that goes untested.
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_reconciler_shadow_package_ordering.py add a second test that, after the engine-first seed, sets sys.modules['rebar_reconciler.classify'] to a module object lacking __path__ (e.g. importlib.util.module_from_spec of the engine classify.py), calls _load_bridge()(), and asserts importlib.import_module('rebar_reconciler.classify') now has __path__ (the stale module was evicted).
